title: Whether he was the first Black saxophonist in Los Angeles
summary: Willard asks if the article's claim is true; Howard says another saxophonist preceded him.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Any other points you have here?
The article makes the statement that Paul Howard was the first Negro saxophonist in Los Angeles. Is that true?
No, there was another guy ahead, in front of me.
(inaudible) the mike up please?
Yeah, another fellow in front of me. And I can't think of his name. If I could just think of his name. Wait a minute. Played the Great saxophone-- That was somebody before you?
Somebody before you?
Yeah. I can't think of his name. And you've heard him then a hundred times.
Umm.
And I bet you couldn't think of it.
Would he be a famous saxophone player?
Naw, he never got that famous. Got rowdier and louder (laughter), but I can't--
Was he anybody that ever was known
well at 767? Was he in the union when the union started?
Uh-uh, no, no.
Well, maybe we'll think of his name later. But there was only one black saxophone player here in Los Angeles until you got here? Is that right?
There was only one.
But there were other, a few other Negro musicians, were there not? Nobody had taken up saxophone?
Nobody had done what, dear?
Nobody had taken up saxophone?
No.
There were other Negro musicians?
Yeah, there were other musicians. Uh-uh-uh.
